reviewed_registry.note: v1 is read-only here. This file records verdicts for the correction task; it does not edit claims.json.

scope: EH-02 phase 3b: Study 02 runs 20260920T234953Z, 20260921T183722Z, 20260921T205212Z and Study 03 run 20260921T231328Z; AM-01..AM-04 and the dev-check control evidence.

verdicts.reason: Derived from the Study 02 v1 matrix run 20260913T021206Z, which this phase-3b validation does not re-measure. Not contradicted; no verdict.

accepted_clauses: A ticketing database chosen only to prevent overbooking cannot report refunds at all: r05 is unanswerable and r01/r03 partial in 14 of 15 designs because cancellation erases the sale.
The append-only ledger that fixes it costs about +33-35% storage.
rejected_clauses: 8x load time: the reports run measured pg-single X1 load at 6410 ms vs P3 826 ms (7.8x), but the same loader code measured 1062/1106 ms vs 881/868 ms in runs 20260921T183722Z/20260921T205212Z (1.21x/1.27x). Empty harness diff between the commits. The multiplier is a single-observation outlier and must not be published.
verdicts.reason: Answerability and storage are corroborated; the load multiplier is contradicted by two sibling runs of the same pair and code.
verdicts.follow_up: Re-measure a load-only P3/X1 repeat (verify phase only, small, pg-single) before any load-cost number is published; otherwise publish storage (+33-35%) only.

accepted_clauses: At 128 buyers the ledger costs 1.1-2.3x of the sell-out race on PostgreSQL (verified 1.06-2.35x with 3-37% spreads) and 1.8-2.2x on YugabyteDB (verified 1.68-2.21x).
2.1-2.5x on the refund itself (verified yb-single cancel 575->271, yb-cluster3 404->164).
The organiser's unrelated edit is delayed up to 5x.
verdicts.reason: Every figure re-derived from results/20260921T205212Z/*/x1_cas_ledger.json. Scoped to one small, closed-loop, quota-bound run at 128 buyers; must carry that scope and must not be extrapolated to 32 buyers.

accepted_clauses: On PostgreSQL this 32-buyer run cannot be trusted on the ledger-cost axis because P3's own trials disagree by 92-283%.
rejected_clauses: YugabyteDB '1.7-2.1x': the run's own tables give 2.05-5.73x on yb-single and 1.67-3.00x on yb-cluster3, i.e. 1.7-5.7x; 1.7-2.1x is the sibling run's (20260921T205212Z) range. The header range must be widened to the run data or scoped to the 1k/10k/100k tiers.
verdicts.reason: Re-derived from the 3b-2 report tables. The signed analysis body already says '1.7x to 5.7x'; only the headline (the source of this claim) understates it.
verdicts.follow_up: Correct the derived claim's range; keep the PostgreSQL self-limitation verbatim. Record in the correction ledger that the 3b-2 analysis's conclusion-3 cancel figures (575->271, 404->164) are the sibling run's; 3b-2's own are 579->270 and 485->157.

verdicts.reason: Study 03 v1 run 20260915T002411Z, a different digest and question (holds/refusals/publishing). This read-only reports run neither confirms nor contradicts it.

accepted_clauses: In every design of study 03 the report that would size the 40-minute hold window is unanswerable (r06, verified in all 14 designs of all three topologies).
On YugabyteDB the section document answers the 100k-seat map 4.5-11x faster than per-seat rows (verified: yb-single 3102 vs 679/273; yb-cluster3 4294 vs 942).
The section-sharded variant collapses point lookups to 26 ops/s (verified r02 = 26.4 on yb-single L3; L2 1520; row designs ~4900/5700).
verdicts.reason: Re-derived from results/20260921T231328Z/<topology>/<design>.json. Scoped to one small, read-only, single-trial, quota-bound run; differences below ~1.8x are not attributable.
Same structural r06 finding; it is a schema limitation, not a missing measurement, and is correctly labelled a gap.
Its whole content is 'the v2 operational-report runs are complete but their HIGH validation is still open'. This review is that validation, so the claim is no longer true.
verdicts.follow_up: Drop or supersede claim-gap-04 in the v2 registry; replace it with the validation state if a coverage marker is wanted.
